Our minute-by-minute report for Tottenham v Aston Villa is live! Join Daniel Gallan.
The team news is in:

Tottenham XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van De Ven, Robertson, Tonali, Bentancur, Savio, Fernandes, Marmoush, Solanke.
Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Udogie, Gray, Bergvall, Kudus.
Pedro Porro returns for Spurs and slots in at right-back in place of Archie Gray. Sandro Tonali also returns to the starting line-up in place of Conor Gallagher.

Aston Villa XI: Suzuki, Wan-Bissaka, Mings, Lindelof, Ruggeri, Joao Gomes, Kamara, McGinn, Buendia, Manzambi, Jackson.
Subs: Wright, Cash, Harwoo-Bellis, Barkley, Garnacho, Abraham, Mbaye, Bogarde, Hemmings.

Summer signing Johan Manzambi makes his debut! Looked a very exciting player with Switzerland at the World Cup. Joao Gomes returns after his ban following an opening-day red card. Matteo Ruggeri and Tyrone Mings are also included with Ross Barkley dropping to the bench, despite his goal against Coventry in the League Cup.

Turns out Emi Martinez is less the new Petr Cech and more the new Dave Beasant. Some of us saw it coming amidst those 'signing of the window' plaudits here and elsewhere. Long way to go yet, but he's been on the slide for years.
https://avatar.guim.co.uk/user/2620971
Emi Martínez has conceded 10 goals in four matches since joining Chelsea and while he hasn’t been at his best, I think the Blues’ defensive woes are a collective problem.

Looking back at the three goals that Brentford scored last night, I’m not sure he is at fault for any of them (potentially could have come for the corner that led to Bees’ first goal?!). He actually made an excellent one-on-one stop top deny Kevin Schade and was helpless to prevent Thiago tucking in the rebound.

It remains an interesting goalkeeper situation at Chelsea. Robert Sánchez has been sent on loan to Como, with Cesc Fabregas excited to have his compatriot in his squad: “Robert Sánchez is a player who comes from a very important team, he’s won trophies and is under constant pressure. There, you have to always win. It was a great opportunity to always win. Since he’s arrived, it’s perfect for me; we didn’t expect it at the start.”

Xabi Alonso does have the option of Mike Penders, who is widely seen as Chelsea’s No 1 in the long-term. The Belgian impressed at Strasbourg last season and is very good with his feet, an area that is not the strongest for Martínez. Penders is the No 2 and will play games in the cups, but it will be interesting to see if Chelsea improve defensively with Martínez in the Premier League.
